prompt.en: Explain why cells evolved organelles instead of carrying out all of their tasks in one shared open space.

label.en: A cell performs many tasks at the same time

level1.en: Think about everything a living cell needs to do at once — producing energy, building molecules, breaking down waste, and more.

clue.en: A cell is constantly running many different jobs in parallel, not one after another.

level2Template.en: A living cell is constantly performing many different ___ at the same time.

label.en: Doing everything in one shared space causes interference

level1.en: What would go wrong if every one of these tasks happened together in a single crowded space?

clue.en: Like machines crammed into one factory room, the different chemical processes would get in each other's way.

level2Template.en: If all of a cell's activities happened in one crowded space, they would ___ with one another.

level1.en: What evolved inside the cell to give each task its own separate work area?

clue.en: These are specialized structures surrounded by their own membrane, each dedicated to one particular job — their name literally means 'little organs'.

level2Template.en: Evolution solved this by creating specialized, membrane-bound compartments called ___, each dedicated to a particular task.
